snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\bar\alpha=\alpha\wedge1\), \(\bar\beta=\beta\wedge1\), \(\bar s=s\wedge1\), \(k=(2\alpha+1)^{-1}\), and suppose \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\). Put
\[
z_*=\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\bar\beta\ge\bar\alpha,\\
\max\{\alpha/2,\alpha-\bar\beta\},&\bar\beta<\bar\alpha\text{ and }\bar\beta\ge\alpha/(2\alpha+1),\\
\alpha\bar\alpha/(\bar\alpha+\bar\beta),&\bar\beta<\bar\alpha\text{ and }\bar\beta<\alpha/(2\alpha+1),
\end{cases}
\]
\(m_*=\max\{z_*,\alpha-z_*\}\), and \(\varrho_*=\max\{z_*/\bar\alpha,(\alpha-z_*)/\bar\beta\}\). With \(h\asymp n^{-k}\), \(b\asymp n^{-k\varrho_*}\), and \(\delta\asymp n^{-km_*/\bar s}\), the envelope in \(\mathrm{lem:beta\text{-}free\text{-}master\text{-}risk}\) is \(O(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)})\).

Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), and \(S_0=s\wedge1\). The four-fold estimator \(\widehat\theta_{h,b,\delta}\) specified by \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{bf}}\) is Borel measurable. There are constants \(C,c_1,h_0,b_0,\delta_0>0\), independent of \(n\), such that, whenever \(0<h\le h_0\), \(0<b\le b_0\), \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), and \(nb\delta^d\ge C\),
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)\le C\left[h^{2\alpha}+\left\{(u+h^{A_0})(v+h^{B_0})\right\}^2+\frac1{nh}+\frac1n+\exp(-c_1nh)\right],
\]
where
\[

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) into cubes \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) into cubes \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(0<\beta<\beta^{\prime}<\infty\) and every admissible \(\alpha,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0\) such that the rough tuple satisfies \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), none depending on \(n\), such that for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1\le
\frac{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)}{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)}
\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{C_{\mathrm{low}}}.
\]
No oracle-region condition on \(\beta^{\prime}\) is required.

Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) into cubes \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) into cubes \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

Let \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)\), and impose consistency and conditional exchangeability. Suppose additionally that these causal assumptions admit a compatible continuous conditional-mean version: there is a jointly Borel function \(m_P:[0,1]\times[0,1]^d\to[-M_Y,M_Y]\) such that \(m_P(a,\cdot)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E[Y(a)\mid X=\cdot]\) for every \(a\), both \(a\mapsto m_P(a,x)\) and \(a\mapsto\mu_P(a,x)\) are continuous for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\), and
\[
\mu_P(a,x)=m_P(a,x)
\]
for \(\pi_P(a\mid x)\,da\,dP_X(x)\)-almost every \((a,x)\). Then the observed-data partial mean is causally identified at the fixed dose:
\[
\theta_P(t_0)=\int\mu_P(t_0,x)p_X(x)\,dx=\mathbb E[Y(t_0)].
\]
The compatible-version condition is essential at a singleton dose; consistency and exchangeability alone do not select a conditional-mean version at the null event \(A=t_0\).

\[

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

\[

=

\]

\[

\]

\quad \delta_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/S_0},

the envelope in \(\mathrm{lem:localized\text{-}polynomial\text{-}master\text{-}risk}\) is \(O(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)})\).

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

\[

\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]

\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), suppose \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), and put \(C_0=2\alpha+1\). On \(I=[(\alpha-B_0)_+,A_0]\), define
\[
F_\mu(z)=\frac{dz}{C_0-z/A_0-2z},
\qquad
F_\pi(z)=\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{C_0-(\alpha-z)/B_0-2(\alpha-z)},
\]
where both denominators are required to be positive. Then
\[
\min_{z\in I}\max\{F_\mu(z),F_\pi(z)\}=g(\alpha,\beta,d),
\]
with \(g\) given by the closed form in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\text{-}threshold}\). The minimizer is the unique crossing of the two functions. It lies below \(\alpha/2\) when \(A_0<B_0\), equals \(\alpha/2\) when \(A_0=B_0\), and lies above \(\alpha/2\) when \(A_0>B_0\). The three formulas agree continuously at \(A_0=B_0\). Moreover, this separated-pilot threshold is no larger than the shared-pilot threshold, and the inequality can be strict.

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

Let \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)\), and impose consistency and conditional exchangeability. Suppose additionally that these causal assumptions admit a compatible continuous conditional-mean version: there is a jointly Borel function \(m_P:[0,1]\times[0,1]^d\to[-M_Y,M_Y]\) such that \(m_P(a,\cdot)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E[Y(a)\mid X=\cdot]\) for every \(a\), both \(a\mapsto m_P(a,x)\) and \(a\mapsto\mu_P(a,x)\) are continuous for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\), and
\[
\mu_P(a,x)=m_P(a,x)
\]

\[

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):

\right\}.
\]

\[
h\asymp n^{-k},
\quad b_\mu\asymp n^{-kz_*/A_0},
\quad \delta_\mu\asymp n^{-kz_*/S_0},
\]
\[
b_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/B_0},
\quad \delta_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/S_0},
\]
the envelope in \(\mathrm{lem:localized\text{-}polynomial\text{-}master\text{-}risk}\) is \(O(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)})\).

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

For the separate pilots in \(\mathrm{def:beta\text{-}free\text{-}handle}\), the random variables \(U\) and \(V\) defined in \(\mathrm{lem:separate\text{-}slice\text{-}pilot\text{-}mse}\) are independent under every \(P\). Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E_P[U^2V^2]=\mathbb E_P[U^2]\mathbb E_P[V^2]\le C u^2v^2.
\]

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) into cubes \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) into cubes \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

snapshot.stmt: Suppose \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\). Then for every admissible \(M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0\), there are \(0<C_-\le C_+<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that \[C_-r_n(\alpha)\le\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)\le C_+r_n(\alpha).\] On this oracle region, if \(\beta<\alpha\), the same-class minimax exponent is strictly larger than the \(2(\alpha\wedge\beta)/(2(\alpha\wedge\beta)+1)\) exponent in the treatment-smoothing term of Bonvini and Kennedy's conditional-risk Theorem 3.1; this is not a contradiction of that estimator-specific upper bound.

defs.def:holder-class: \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)=\{P\in\mathcal P(Z):\text{ there exist designated versions }(\mu_P,\pi_P,p_X)\text{ satisfying }\mathrm{ass:mu-version},\mathrm{ass:pi-version},\mathrm{ass:px-version},\mathrm{ass:bounded-outcome},\mathrm{ass:positivity-lower},\mathrm{ass:positivity-upper},\mathrm{ass:px-bounded},\mathrm{ass:mu-a-holder},\mathrm{ass:pi-a-holder},\mathrm{ass:mu-x-holder},\mathrm{ass:pi-x-holder}\}\). Hölder order \(q>0\) on a cube means \(\lfloor q\rfloor\) continuous coordinate derivatives and a \(q-\lfloor q\rfloor\) Hölder remainder, with the usual bounded-derivative convention when \(q\in\mathbb N\); the \(x\)-conditions are coordinatewise. defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(0<\beta<\beta^{\prime}<\infty\) and every admissible \(\alpha,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0\) such that the rough tuple satisfies \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), none depending on \(n\), such that for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1\le
\frac{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)}{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)}
\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{C_{\mathrm{low}}}.
\]
No oracle-region condition on \(\beta^{\prime}\) is required.

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. \[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). \[

\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]

\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]

\[

\]

\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

\[

=
\frac{1}{2a_0}+\frac{d}{4q_0}
+
\left(\frac12-\frac{b_0}{a_0}\right)_+
\min\left\{\frac{1}{2b_0},\frac{d}{2q_0}\right\},
\qquad

=
\frac{1}{1+m_{\mathrm{hist}}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)}.
\]

\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le
C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-R_{\mathrm{hist}}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)}.
\]

\[

\]
The displayed achievable exponent is independent of \(\beta\) on the subregion \(b_0\ge a_0/2\), where
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)
=
\left(1+\frac{1}{2a_0}+\frac{d}{4q_0}\right)^{-1}.
\]

\[

\]
for \(\pi_P(a\mid x)\,da\,dP_X(x)\)-almost every \((a,x)\). Then the observed-data partial mean is causally identified at the fixed dose:
\[

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[

\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

Put \(a_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(b_0=\beta\wedge1\), and \(q_0=s\wedge1\), and define
\[

\left[

\min\left\{\frac{1}{2b_0},\frac{d}{2q_0}\right\}
\right]^{-1}.
\]

\[

\le
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le
C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-R_{\mathrm{hist}}}.
\]

\[

\left\{1+\frac{1}{2(\alpha\wedge1)}+\frac{d}{4(s\wedge1)}\right\}^{-1}.
\]

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

\[

=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.

\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)\), and impose consistency and conditional exchangeability. Suppose additionally that these causal assumptions admit a compatible continuous conditional-mean version: there is a jointly Borel function \(m_P:[0,1]\times[0,1]^d\to[-M_Y,M_Y]\) such that \(m_P(a,\cdot)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E[Y(a)\mid X=\cdot]\) for every \(a\), both \(a\mapsto m_P(a,x)\) and \(a\mapsto\mu_P(a,x)\) are continuous for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\), and
\[
\mu_P(a,x)=m_P(a,x)
\]
for \(\pi_P(a\mid x)\,da\,dP_X(x)\)-almost every \((a,x)\). Then the observed-data partial mean is causally identified at the fixed dose:
\[
\theta_P(t_0)=\int\mu_P(t_0,x)p_X(x)\,dx=\mathbb E[Y(t_0)].
\]
The compatible-version condition is essential at a singleton dose; consistency and exchangeability alone do not select a conditional-mean version at the null event \(A=t_0\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(0<\beta<\beta^{\prime}<\infty\) and every admissible \(\alpha,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0\) such that the rough tuple satisfies \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), none depending on \(n\), such that for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)
\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1\le
\frac{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)}{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)}
\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{C_{\mathrm{low}}}.
\]
No oracle-region condition on \(\beta^{\prime}\) is required.

defs.def:minimax-mse: \(\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)=\inf_{\widehat\theta\in\mathfrak T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,pbar,c,t_0)}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\theta-\theta_P(t_0))^2]\), where the supremum is over the nonempty class certified by \(\mathrm{prop:class-nonempty}\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt: Suppose \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\). Then for every admissible \(M_Y,L,c,t_0\), there are \(0<C_-\le C_+<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that \[C_-r_n(\alpha)\le\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\le C_+r_n(\alpha).\] On this oracle region, if \(\beta<\alpha\), the same-class minimax exponent is strictly larger than the \(2(\alpha\wedge\beta)/(2(\alpha\wedge\beta)+1)\) exponent in the treatment-smoothing term of Bonvini and Kennedy's conditional-risk Theorem 3.1; this is not a contradiction of that estimator-specific upper bound.

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

For parameter tuples in either residual region
\[
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)<\alpha
\]
or
\[
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\qquad s\wedge1<g(\alpha,\beta,d),
\]

\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\asymp n^{-\rho(\alpha,\beta,s,d)}?
\]
If so, what is that exponent and in which subregions, if any, is it independent of \(\beta\)?

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]

\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],

\[

\quad b_\mu\asymp n^{-kz_*/A_0},
\quad \delta_\mu\asymp n^{-kz_*/S_0},
\]
\[
b_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/B_0},
\quad \delta_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/S_0},

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

For every \(0<\beta<\beta^{\prime}<\infty\) and every admissible \(\alpha,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0\) such that the rough tuple satisfies \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), none depending on \(n\), such that for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[

\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1\le
\frac{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}
\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{C_{\mathrm{low}}}.

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). \[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]

\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]

\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

\[

=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):

\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

For every \(0<\beta<\beta^{\prime}<\infty\) and every admissible \(\alpha,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0\) such that the rough tuple satisfies \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), none depending on \(n\), such that for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1\le
\frac{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}
\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{C_{\mathrm{low}}}.
\]
No oracle-region condition on \(\beta^{\prime}\) is required.

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]

\[

\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]

\end{cases}

The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

\right\}.
\]

Let \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\), and impose consistency, Assumption~\texttt{ass:potential-outcome-path-typing}, and process-level conditional exchangeability. Suppose additionally that there is a jointly Borel function \(m_P:[0,1]\times[0,1]^d\to[-M_Y,M_Y]\) such that \(m_P(a,\cdot)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E[Y(a)\mid X=\cdot]\) for every \(a\), and \(a\mapsto m_P(a,x)\) is continuous at \(t_0\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\). Then the causal assumptions imply
\[
\mu_P(a,x)=m_P(a,x)
\]
for \(da\,dP_X(x)\)-almost every \((a,x)\), and the observed-data partial mean is causally identified at the fixed dose:
\[
\theta_P(t_0)=\int\mu_P(t_0,x)p_X(x)\,dx=\mathbb E[Y(t_0)].
\]
Without the continuity-at-\(t_0\) condition, consistency, measurable path typing, and process-level conditional exchangeability alone do not identify the causal mean at the null event \(A=t_0\).

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

\right\}.
\]

\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le C\left\{h^{2\bar\alpha}+\delta^{4\bar s}+\delta^{2\bar s}h^{2\bar\beta}+\frac1{nh\delta^d}+\frac1n\right\}.
\]

\[
R(u,v)=\min\{2\bar\alpha u,4\bar s v,2\bar s v+2\bar\beta u,1-u-dv,1\}.
\]

\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

Let \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\), let \(V_k\) be the regular-grid space of coordinatewise piecewise polynomials of degree \(\lfloor s\rfloor\), with dimension at most \(C_dk\), and let \(\Pi_{k,P_X}\) be the orthogonal projection onto its image in \(L_2(P_X)\). For \(f=\mu_P(t_0,\cdot)\), \(q=\pi_P(t_0\mid\cdot)\), and arbitrary \(\widetilde f,\widetilde q\in V_k\),
\[
\lVert(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(f-\widetilde f)\rVert_{L_2(P_X)}
+\lVert(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(q-\widetilde q)\rVert_{L_2(P_X)}
\le Ck^{-s/d},
\]
and consequently
\[
\left\lvert\left\langle(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(f-\widetilde f),(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(q-\widetilde q)\right\rangle_{P_X}\right\rvert
\le Ck^{-2s/d}.
\]
If \(\Pi_{k,P_X}(x,x')\) is any orthonormal-basis kernel for this finite-rank projection and \(X_1,X_2\) are independent with law \(P_X\), then
\[
\mathbb E[\Pi_{k,P_X}(X_1,X_2)^2]=\operatorname{rank}(\Pi_{k,P_X})\le C_dk.
\]
The constants do not require a density bound, density lower bound, or smoothness condition on \(p_X\).

snapshot.stmt:
Under the proposed low-covariate-smoothness tuning
\[
h\asymp n^{-4s/\{\alpha(4s+d)+4s\}},
\qquad
k\asymp(nh)^{2d/(4s+d)},
\]
one has
\[
k\asymp n^{2\alpha d/\{\alpha(4s+d)+4s\}},
\]
so \(k/n\to\infty\) exactly when \(s<\alpha d/\{4(\alpha+1)\}\). In particular, at \((\alpha,d,s)=(1,1,0.1)\),
\[
h\asymp n^{-2/9},\qquad nh\asymp n^{7/9},\qquad k\asymp n^{10/9}>n.
\]
Every empirical Gram projection formed from \(n\) covariate observations has rank at most \(n\), and therefore cannot be an invertible rank-\(k\) empirical projection in this subregion.

Put \(a_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(b_0=\beta\wedge1\), and \(q_0=s\wedge1\), and define
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}=
\left[
1+\frac1{2a_0}+\frac d{4q_0}
+\left(\frac12-\frac{b_0}{a_0}\right)_+
\min\left\{\frac1{2b_0},\frac d{2q_0}\right\}
\right]^{-1}.
\]
Then the largest exponent obtainable by optimizing the two power tunings in Lemma~\texttt{lem:explicit-histogram-window-upper} is exactly \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}\). In particular, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le
C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-R_{\mathrm{hist}}}.
\]
Moreover, \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}\) is independent of \(\beta\) whenever \(b_0\ge a_0/2\), in which case
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}=
\left\{1+\frac1{2(\alpha\wedge1)}+\frac d{4(s\wedge1)}\right\}^{-1}.
\]
For every admissible tuple, \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}<2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\), so this is a loose minimax bracket and not an exact deficient-region rate.

\qquad

\]

\[

snapshot.stmt:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), and \(S_0=s\wedge1\), and define
\[
E_\mu=\left(2+A_0^{-1}+dS_0^{-1}\right)^{-1},
\qquad
E_\pi=\left(2+B_0^{-1}+dS_0^{-1}\right)^{-1}.
\]
Define the optimized separated-pilot exponent by the explicit one-dimensional program
\[
R_{\mathrm{sep}}
=
\max_{0\le\gamma\le1}
\min\left\{
2\alpha\gamma,
1-\gamma,
2\left[\min\{A_0\gamma,E_\mu\}+\min\{B_0\gamma,E_\pi\}\right]
\right\},
\]
and define
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=
\left[
1+\frac1{2A_0}+\frac d{4S_0}
+\left(\frac12-\frac{B_0}{A_0}\right)_+
\min\left\{\frac1{2B_0},\frac d{2S_0}\right\}
\right]^{-1},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{ach}}=\max\{R_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{hist}}\}.
\]
For every admissible tuple there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le
C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-R_{\mathrm{ach}}}.
\]
The value \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the largest polynomial exponent furnished by power tuning the frozen separated-pilot master-risk bound, and \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}\) is the largest exponent furnished by power tuning Lemma~\texttt{lem:explicit-histogram-window-upper}. Moreover,
\[
R_{\mathrm{sep}}=\frac{2\alpha}{2\alpha+1}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega,
\]
whereas \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}<2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\) for every admissible tuple. Hence \(R_{\mathrm{ach}}<2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\) whenever either \((\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)<\alpha\), or \((\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha\) and \(s\wedge1<g(\alpha,\beta,d)\). The regressogram exponent is independent of \(\beta\) whenever \(B_0\ge A_0/2\), and all three achievable exponents \(R_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{hist}},R_{\mathrm{ach}}\) are independent of the numerical value of \(\beta\) on \(\beta\ge1\); neither fact by itself establishes minimax \(\beta\)-invariance in a residual region.

defs.def:minimax-mse: \(\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)=\inf_{\widehat\theta\in\mathfrak T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\theta-\theta_P(t_0))^2]\), where the supremum is over the nonempty class certified by \(\mathrm{prop:class-nonempty}\).
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

\[

=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

Let \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\), let \(V_k\) be the regular-grid space of coordinatewise piecewise polynomials of degree \(\lfloor s\rfloor\), with dimension at most \(C_dk\), and let \(\Pi_{k,P_X}\) be the orthogonal projection onto its image in \(L_2(P_X)\). For \(f=\mu_P(t_0,\cdot)\), \(q=\pi_P(t_0\mid\cdot)\), and arbitrary \(\widetilde f,\widetilde q\in V_k\),
\[
\lVert(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(f-\widetilde f)\rVert_{L_2(P_X)}
+\lVert(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(q-\widetilde q)\rVert_{L_2(P_X)}
\le Ck^{-s/d},
\]
and consequently
\[
\left\lvert\left\langle(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(f-\widetilde f),(I-\Pi_{k,P_X})(q-\widetilde q)\right\rangle_{P_X}\right\rvert
\le Ck^{-2s/d}.
\]
If \(\Pi_{k,P_X}(x,x')\) is any orthonormal-basis kernel for this finite-rank projection and \(X_1,X_2\) are independent with law \(P_X\), then
\[
\mathbb E[\Pi_{k,P_X}(X_1,X_2)^2]=\operatorname{rank}(\Pi_{k,P_X})\le C_dk.
\]
The constants do not require a density bound, density lower bound, or smoothness condition on \(p_X\).

Under the proposed low-covariate-smoothness tuning
\[
h\asymp n^{-4s/\{\alpha(4s+d)+4s\}},
\qquad
k\asymp(nh)^{2d/(4s+d)},
\]

\[
k\asymp n^{2\alpha d/\{\alpha(4s+d)+4s\}},
\]

\[
h\asymp n^{-2/9},\qquad nh\asymp n^{7/9},\qquad k\asymp n^{10/9}>n.
\]
Every empirical Gram projection formed from \(n\) covariate observations has rank at most \(n\), and therefore cannot be an invertible rank-\(k\) empirical projection in this subregion.

\[

=

\max\left\{

\right\}.

\[

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[

\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]

\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]

\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,

\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]

=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]

\[

\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). \[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]

\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]

\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]

\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
