\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):

\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), and \(S_0=s\wedge1\), and define
\[
E_\mu=\left(2+A_0^{-1}+dS_0^{-1}\right)^{-1},
\qquad
E_\pi=\left(2+B_0^{-1}+dS_0^{-1}\right)^{-1}.
\]
Define the optimized separated-pilot exponent by the explicit one-dimensional program
\[
R_{\mathrm{sep}}
=
\max_{0\le\gamma\le1}
\min\left\{
2\alpha\gamma,
1-\gamma,
2\left[\min\{A_0\gamma,E_\mu\}+\min\{B_0\gamma,E_\pi\}\right]
\right\},
\]
and define
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=
\left[
1+\frac1{2A_0}+\frac d{4S_0}
+\left(\frac12-\frac{B_0}{A_0}\right)_+
\min\left\{\frac1{2B_0},\frac d{2S_0}\right\}
\right]^{-1},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{ach}}=\max\{R_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{hist}}\}.
\]
For every admissible tuple there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le
C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-R_{\mathrm{ach}}}.
\]
The value \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the largest polynomial exponent furnished by power tuning the frozen separated-pilot master-risk bound, and \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}\) is the largest exponent furnished by power tuning Lemma~\texttt{lem:explicit-histogram-window-upper}. Moreover,
\[
R_{\mathrm{sep}}=\frac{2\alpha}{2\alpha+1}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega,
\]
whereas \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}<2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\) for every admissible tuple. Hence \(R_{\mathrm{ach}}<2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\) whenever either \((\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)<\alpha\), or \((\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha\) and \(s\wedge1<g(\alpha,\beta,d)\). The regressogram exponent is independent of \(\beta\) whenever \(B_0\ge A_0/2\), and all three achievable exponents \(R_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{hist}},R_{\mathrm{ach}}\) are independent of the numerical value of \(\beta\) on \(\beta\ge1\); neither fact by itself establishes minimax \(\beta\)-invariance in a residual region.

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.
defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The first-order separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

\quad \delta_\mu\asymp n^{-kz_*/S_0},

\quad \delta_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/S_0},

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:

=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

\[

=

\[

\le

\le
C_+r_n(\alpha)
\qquad(n\ge n_0).
\]

\[
\mu_P(a,x)=m_P(a,x)

\[

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(0<c<1\), and put \(B_*=\alpha\vee\beta\) and
\[
r_{\mathrm f}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)
=
\frac{8}{4+2/B_*+d/s}.
\]
For every admissible finite \(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,t_0\), there are constants \(C_{\mathrm f}>0\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), independent of \(n\), such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\ge C_{\mathrm f}n^{-r_{\mathrm f}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)}.
\]
Together with Lemma~\texttt{lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor}, this gives
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\ge
C n^{-\min\{2\alpha/(2\alpha+1),r_{\mathrm f}(\alpha,\beta,s,d)\}}.
\]
The new fuzzy lower bound is strictly stronger than the oracle floor exactly when
\[
\frac ds>4+\frac4\alpha-\frac{2}{\alpha\vee\beta}.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(S_0=s\wedge1\), and \(k=(2\alpha+1)^{-1}\). Suppose \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), and let \(z_*\) be the constrained minimizer in Lemma~\texttt{lem:separated-threshold-optimization}. With
\[
h\asymp n^{-k},
\quad b_\mu\asymp n^{-kz_*/A_0},
\quad \delta_\mu\asymp n^{-kz_*/S_0},
\]
\[
b_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/B_0},
\quad \delta_\pi\asymp n^{-k(\alpha-z_*)/S_0},
\]
the envelope in Lemma~\texttt{lem:localized-polynomial-master-risk} is \(O(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)})\).

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The first-order separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

\]

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\mathcal Q_1(\alpha,d,M_Y,L)\) be the class of Borel probability laws \(P\) of \(Z=(Y,A,X)\), with \(X\in[0,1]^d\), such that \(\lvert Y\rvert\le M_Y\) almost surely, \(A\) is uniform on \([0,1]\) and independent of \(X\), and there is a jointly Borel version \(\mu_P(a,x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) for which every section \(a\mapsto\mu_P(a,x)\) lies in the univariate H\"older ball of order \(\alpha\) and radius \(L\), uniformly in \(x\). The marginal law \(P_X\) is an arbitrary Borel probability law; no Lebesgue-density requirement, no smoothness of \(x\mapsto\mu_P(t_0,x)\), and no treatment-density smoothness are imposed. Define
\[
\mathcal N_n(\alpha,d,M_Y,L,t_0)
=
\inf_{\widehat\theta\in\mathfrak T_n}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q_1(\alpha,d,M_Y,L)}
\mathbb E_P\left[\left\{\widehat\theta-\int_{[0,1]^d}\mu_P(t_0,x)\,P_X(dx)\right\}^2\right].
\]
For every admissible \(\alpha,d,M_Y,L,t_0\), there are constants \(0<C_-\le C_+<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
C_-r_n(\alpha)
\le
\mathcal N_n(\alpha,d,M_Y,L,t_0)
\le
C_+r_n(\alpha)
\qquad(n\ge n_0).
\]
For every \(\beta,s>0\), \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,1,t_0)\) is a proper subset of \(\mathcal Q_1(\alpha,d,M_Y,L)\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(0<\beta<\beta^{\prime}<\infty\) and every admissible \(\alpha,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0\) such that the rough tuple satisfies \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), none depending on \(n\), such that for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1\le
\frac{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}
\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{C_{\mathrm{low}}}.
\]
No oracle-region condition on \(\beta^{\prime}\) is required.

Suppose \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\). Then for every admissible \(M_Y,L,c,t_0\), there are \(0<C_-\le C_+<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that \[C_-r_n(\alpha)\le\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\le C_+r_n(\alpha).\] On this oracle region, if \(\beta<\alpha\), the same-class minimax exponent is strictly larger than the \(2(\alpha\wedge\beta)/(2(\alpha\wedge\beta)+1)\) exponent in the treatment-smoothing term of Bonvini and Kennedy's conditional-risk Theorem 3.1; this is not a contradiction of that estimator-specific upper bound.

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
defs.def:oracle-region:
The first-order separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(0<c<1\). For parameter tuples in either residual region
\[
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)<\alpha
\]
or
\[
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\qquad s\wedge1<g(\alpha,\beta,d),
\]
does there exist an exact polynomial-rate exponent \(\rho(\alpha,\beta,s,d)\) such that
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\asymp n^{-\rho(\alpha,\beta,s,d)}?
\]
If so, what is that exponent and in which subregions, if any, is it independent of \(\beta\)?

snapshot.stmt:
For the two slice pilots in \(\mathrm{def:beta\text{-}free\text{-}handle}\), put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(S_0=s\wedge1\),
\[
U=\lVert\widehat\mu_0-\mu_P(t_0,\cdot)\rVert_{L_2(P_X)},
\qquad
V=\lVert\widehat\pi_0-\pi_P(t_0\mid\cdot)\rVert_{L_2(P_X)},
\]
and
\[
u=\delta_\mu^{S_0}+b_\mu^{A_0}+(nb_\mu\delta_\mu^d)^{-1/2},
\qquad
v=\delta_\pi^{S_0}+b_\pi^{B_0}+(nb_\pi\delta_\pi^d)^{-1/2}.
\]
There are constants \(C,C_0<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, whenever \(nb_\mu\delta_\mu^d\ge C_0\) and \(nb_\pi\delta_\pi^d\ge C_0\),
\[
\mathbb E_PU^2\le Cu^2,
\qquad
\mathbb E_PV^2\le Cv^2.
\]

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

Let \(\widetilde\mu\) and \(\widetilde\pi\) be arbitrary Borel functions with \(\lvert\widetilde\mu\rvert\le M_Y\) and \(c/2\le\widetilde\pi\le2/c\). Write \(v_a=\widetilde\mu(a,\cdot)-\mu_P(a,\cdot)\), \(e_a=\widetilde\pi(a\mid\cdot)-\pi_P(a\mid\cdot)\), \(\bar e_a=P_Xe_a\), \(f_a=P_X\pi_P(a\mid\cdot)\), \(\widetilde f_a=P_X\widetilde\pi(a\mid\cdot)\), and \(\widetilde m_a=P_X\widetilde\mu(a,\cdot)\). For \(\widetilde\xi=\{\widetilde f_A/\widetilde\pi(A\mid X)\}\{Y-\widetilde\mu(A,X)\}+\widetilde m_A\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[\widetilde\xi\mid A=a]=\theta_P(a)+B(a),
\quad

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]

\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

\le C\left\{h^{2\bar\alpha}+\delta^{4\bar s}+\delta^{2\bar s}h^{2\bar\beta}+\frac1{nh\delta^d}+\frac1n\right\}.

\[

defs.def:beta-free-handle:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]

\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

Fix \(0<c<1\), and suppose either \((\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)<\alpha\) or \((\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha\) and \(s\wedge1<g(\alpha,\beta,d)\). Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(S_0=s\wedge1\),
\[

\]
\[

\]
\[

\qquad R_{\mathrm{ach}}=\max\{R_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{hist}}\},
\]
and
\[

\]

\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-r_{\mathrm{low}}}\le\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-R_{\mathrm{ach}}}\qquad(n\ge n_0).
\]

If an exact polynomial exponent \(\rho\) exists, then \(R_{\mathrm{ach}}\le\rho\le r_{\mathrm{low}}\); wherever the endpoints agree, the exact exponent is their common value. The lower exponent is independent of the numerical value of \(\beta\) for \(\beta\le\alpha\); \(R_{\mathrm{hist}}\) is independent of that value when \(\beta\wedge1\ge(\alpha\wedge1)/2\); and all displayed achievable exponents are independent of that value on \(\beta\ge1\). Thus the frozen assumptions determine this explicit bracket, but do not in general determine an exact exponent outside the endpoint-equality subregions.

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

defs.def:oracle-threshold:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

snapshot.stmt: Suppose \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\). Then for every admissible \(M_Y,L,c,t_0\), there are \(0<C_-\le C_+<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that \[C_-r_n(\alpha)\le\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\le C_+r_n(\alpha).\] On this oracle region, if \(\beta<\alpha\), the same-class minimax exponent \(2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\) is numerically larger than the exponent \(2\beta/(2\beta+1)\) obtained by balancing the treatment-smoothing component of Bonvini and Kennedy's conditional estimator-risk bound with its leading variance order. The models and guarantees differ: the present result is a uniform minimax statement over the displayed class, whereas theirs is a conditional bound for a specified estimator. This is a contrast between unlike guarantees, not a strict tightening or estimator-domination claim.

defs.def:holder-class: \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)=\{P\in\mathcal P(Z):\text{ there exist designated versions }(\mu_P,\pi_P,p_X)\text{ satisfying }\mathrm{ass:mu-version},\mathrm{ass:pi-version},\mathrm{ass:px-version},\mathrm{ass:bounded-outcome},\mathrm{ass:positivity-lower},\mathrm{ass:positivity-upper},\mathrm{ass:mu-a-holder},\mathrm{ass:pi-a-holder},\mathrm{ass:mu-x-holder},\mathrm{ass:pi-x-holder}\}\). Throughout, a H\"older ball of order \(q>0\) and radius \(L\) means the corresponding H\"older seminorm ball: \(L\) bounds all required positive-order coordinate derivatives and the terminal H\"older modulus or Taylor remainder, but it does not bound the zeroth-order supremum norm. defs.def:minimax-mse: \(\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)=\inf_{\widehat\theta\in\mathfrak T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\theta-\theta_P(t_0))^2]\), where the supremum is over the nonempty class certified by \(\mathrm{prop:class-nonempty}\).

The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).
